slides.title: VT-MUSE: Multimodal Unified Sequential Visuotactile Representation Learning for Manipulation
slides.highlight: VT-MUSE introduces a two-stage framework for learning unified visuotactile representations that capture temporal evolution and cross-modal dependencies, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal perception.

card.one_liner: VT-MUSE learns unified sequential visuotactile representations to improve contact-rich robotic manipulation in simulation and real-world.
card.key_idea: A two-stage framework: Stage I aligns modalities via temporal contrast; Stage II uses a conditional variational model to reconstruct masked vision and predict tactile depth changes.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on UniVTAC simulation and physical tasks; outperformed strongest baselines by 16.25 percentage points in simulation and achieved 95% success rate in real-world trials.
card.limitation: Uses fixed sample strides and window sizes; pretraining was limited to 7 tasks, leaving scaling laws for larger task sets unvalidated.

slides.title: HiTac-WAM: A Hierarchical Tactile World Action Model for Contact-Rich Robot Manipulation
slides.tldr: HIERARCHICAL TACTILE WORLD ACTION MODEL FOR ROBOT MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: HiTac-WAM forecasts future tactile states by factorizing contact state, 3D deformation, and slip risk into a directed hierarchy. This approach improves real-robot success rates in contact-rich tasks like USB insertion and chip grasping.

card.one_liner: HiTac-WAM improves contact-rich robot manipulation by forecasting hierarchical tactile consequences to rank and verify actions.
card.key_idea: A world action model that factorizes tactile forecasts into a directed hierarchy (contact $\rightarrow$ deformation $\rightarrow$ slip risk) using stop-gradient conditioning and directed attention masks.
card.evaluation: Tested on chip grasping, blackboard erasing, and USB insertion; achieved 72.2% success rate and 0.921 mean contact F1 score.
card.limitation: Forecast quality on model-generated action chunks was not evaluated separately, and predicted slip risk is not calibrated for online detection.

slides.title: SoftVTBench: A Deformation-Aware Visuo-Tactile Dataset and Benchmark for Deformable-Object Manipulation
slides.highlight: This work introduces a visuo-tactile dataset and benchmark to evaluate how policies physically interact with deformable objects. It is relevant to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception by providing a framework for analyzing the fusion of visual and tactile observations.

card.one_liner: SoftVTBench is a visuo-tactile dataset and benchmark for evaluating physical interaction quality in deformable-object manipulation.
card.key_idea: It pairs policy-visible visuo-tactile streams with evaluator-only FEM states to measure a Deformation-aware Success Rate (DSR) based on calibrated object-specific tolerances.
card.evaluation: Evaluated Diffusion Policy, π0.5, and FastWAM on 4,000 demonstrations across 40 tasks; results show DSR identifies failures that task-success-only metrics miss.
card.limitation: The deformation tolerance is an operational simulation criterion, not a real-world material-failure or damage threshold.

slides.title: The Missing Touch: Spatially Distributed Tactile Feedback Brings Teleoperation Closer to Human Dexterity
slides.highlight: This research demonstrates that spatially distributed tactile feedback reduces the gap between teleoperated and natural human trajectories, supporting the MOSAIC goal of estimating and improving procedural skill through force-based feedback.

card.one_liner: Spatially distributed tactile feedback makes teleoperated movements more natural, consistent, and efficient than low-resolution feedback.
card.key_idea: A 32-DoF cutaneous shape display reproduces localized deformations from a robot's vision-based tactile sensor to the operator's fingertip.
card.evaluation: 12 participants performed button discrimination and peg-rolling tasks; results showed 29–79% reduction in trajectory deviation using DTW metrics.
card.limitation: Evaluated using only a 2-DoF system and two specific tasks; may not generalize to higher-DoF dexterous manipulation.

slides.title: Safety-Critical Bilateral Teleoperation for Omnidirectional Aerial Manipulation Using Force-Sensorless Haptic Feedback
slides.tldr: FORCE-SENSORLESS HAPTIC FEEDBACK FOR AERIAL MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: This framework uses a hierarchical safety filter based on control barrier functions to provide haptic feedback for aerial manipulators without requiring onboard force sensors.

card.one_liner: A safety-critical bilateral teleoperation framework for omnidirectional aerial manipulators using force-sensorless haptic feedback.
card.key_idea: A hierarchical safety filter using Control Barrier Functions (CBFs) adjusts operator commands to ensure tracking error constraints and motor thrust limits, mapping these adjustments to haptic feedback.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via hardware experiments with a hexarotor-based omnidirectional aerial manipulator; results showed stability during free-flight and consistent feedback during physical interaction compared to momentum-based baselines.

slides.title: PRISM: Precision and contact-rich Real-world Industrial Skill dataset with Multimodal sensing
slides.highlight: PRISM provides a large-scale dataset of contact-rich industrial tasks using synchronized RGB-D, force/torque, and tactile sensing, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal perception.

card.one_liner: PRISM is a large-scale multimodal dataset for high-precision, contact-rich industrial robotic manipulation tasks.
card.key_idea: A dataset of 5,000+ trajectories across 25+ tasks, featuring synchronized multi-view RGB-D, 6-axis force/torque, proprioception, and tactile sensing across multiple robot platforms.
card.evaluation: Evaluated using ACT, Diffusion Policy, and $\pi_0$ on real robots; success rates improved with more data and pretraining, though precision remains challenging.
card.limitation: Current imitation learning policies still struggle with dynamic object manipulation and reliable force regulation under tight industrial tolerances.

slides.title: Contact-Rich Robotic Manipulation in Construction via Zero-Shot Learning: A Diffusion Policy-Guided Adaptive Control
slides.highlight: This framework combines diffusion policies with adaptive control to handle uncertain contact dynamics in assembly, aligning with MOSAIC's focus on physics and force-based skill acquisition.

card.one_liner: A framework for zero-shot sim-to-real contact-rich construction assembly using diffusion policies and adaptive control.
card.key_idea: Combines a CNN-based diffusion policy trained on simulation pose/force data with an L1-inspired adaptive controller to correct actions online against unmodeled dynamics.
card.evaluation: Tested on timber joinery, pipe fitting, and truss assembly; achieved 100% success on single tasks and 90-100% on sequential subtasks.

slides.title: Act with Intent: Distilling Behavior Intent for Vision-Language-Action Models
slides.tldr: DISTILLING BEHAVIOR INTENT FOR VLA MODELS
slides.highlight: This work proposes Intention Distillation (INDI) to explicitly model the semantic objective of robot behaviors, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal perception of intent and state.

card.one_liner: Indi improves VLA models by distilling behavior-level intent from a teacher VLM into the action decoder.
card.key_idea: A frozen teacher VLM generates multimodal intent targets from executed behavior; the student decoder learns to recover this intent as a functional intermediate state for action prediction.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on SimplerEnv-Bridge, RoboCasa Kitchen, and real-world tasks using GR00T-N1.7 and π0.5. Results show significant success rate gains, especially on long-horizon tasks.
